assertions.name: bridge_and_cos_factor_differ_by_more_than_four_orders
assertions.source: |rel(bridge_exact_C)| = 0.0536332 vs |rel(cos_model_C)| = 1.27858e-6. The two are not variants of one correction; treating the cos factor as a resummation of the bridge conflates objects of different size.

assertions.name: exact_bridge_is_not_closer_to_F_required_than_truncated
assertions.source: Adopting the exact bridge in place of its O(h) truncation does not move the cos-role sites toward the required correction — it is marginally further away. The discrepancy there is not a truncation error, so it cannot be fixed by de-truncating.

assertions.name: F_required_slope_sign_opposes_every_candidate
assertions.source: dF_required/dq = 2.3355461 > 0 while every candidate slope is negative. The curves cross rather than track, reproducing in the smooth coordinate what the phase coordinate showed — so that finding is not an artifact of the arccos.

description: Measures every proposed Q_β multiplicative correction in the coordinate F = Q_β/Q_A, which is smooth (unlike the phase α, whose square-root branch point 0.062% above q₀ is an artifact of the cos parameterisation). Establishes that the Form-A/Form-B bridge and the ladder's cos factor are DIFFERENT objects: the bridge sits ~5e-2 from what the data requires and the cos factor ~1e-6, because 1+α differs from 1 by α while cos α differs by α²/2 — a size change of 2/|α| ≈ 38. Consequence for 'use the exact bridge everywhere': in the bridge role the exact form is already in use with its truncation error Lean-proved (bridge_first_order_remainder, sorry-free); in the cos role the exact bridge is ~5% wrong, so substituting it would be a regression. The exact bridge is also NOT closer to F_required than the truncation. No fit; nothing wired; nothing derived.
